name: meteors

frames.best_why: Frame 6 catches the most streaks spread across the card; frame 1 shows only one near the top edge.

tagline: Faint shooting stars streak diagonally across a dark, softly glowing card.
summary: A looping shower of thin diagonal light streaks that fall across whatever container it sits in, usually a dark card. It adds slow night-sky motion behind the text.
appearance: A dark, softly rounded card on black with a blurred blue-teal halo leaking out behind its lower edge. Inside sit a small ring icon, a bold white heading, two grey lines of copy and a thin outlined Explore button, crossed by a few pale diagonal streaks.
behaviour: Around twenty thin streaks enter from the top of the card at randomised delays and speeds, drift down-left and fade out near the bottom, looping forever. The whole layer fades in once when it mounts.
demo_content: Card headed "Meteors because they're cool" with two sentences about shooting stars and an Explore button.
search_phrases: shooting stars falling across a card
diagonal streaks of light on loop
decorative backdrop for a call to action
use_when: A dark card or panel needs quiet continuous motion to feel alive without competing with its text.
avoid_when: Light or busy backgrounds: the pale grey streaks disappear and the night-sky mood is lost.
customise: number sets how many streaks run and className adds utility classes. Streak colour, thickness, angle and the five-second loop are fixed in the source.
weight_why: Up to twenty one-pixel spans on a CSS loop inside a single fading wrapper.

a11y.note: The streaks are decorative but not marked aria-hidden, and the loop keeps running under reduced-motion.

issues: Streaks are so thin and pale that they can read as scratches on the dark card.
polish_why: The halo and rounded card are tidy, but the shower itself is too faint to carry the card.
title: Meteors
